To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

caloric restriction activates the plasma membrane red-ox signaling system, which in turn increases cellular resistance to oxidative stress, and that this effect may contribute, at least in part, to the antiaging effects of caloric restrictions.

caloric restriction attenuates vascular oxidative stress by increasing bioavailability of NO through inhibition of NADPH oxidase activity and by increasing expression of the plasma membrane NAD(P)H oxidase, which is responsible for the production of NO and hydrogen peroxide.

caloric restriction attenuates vascular aging by increasing bioavailability of NO and decreasing vascular generation of ROS, which, in turn, activates the NADPH oxidase–dependent Nrf2/ARE pathway, inducing reactive species detoxification systems and suppressing initiation and progression of vascular disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of oxidative stress in the aging of the vasculature and the mechanisms whereby caloric restriction attenuates vascular aging.
the molecular mechanisms that underlie the beneficial effects of caloric restrictions on vascular aging.
the mechanisms by which caloric restriction and related interventions delay the aging process and increase lifespan in mammals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the antiaging cardiovascular benefits of caloric restriction are mediated by attenuation of vascular inflammation, oxidative stress, and mitochondrial dysfunction.
caloric restriction is a potent anti-aging intervention and that it may have the greatest impact on cardiovascular health.
caloric restriction, by attenuating oxidative stress, inhibiting vascular inflammation, and increasing oxidative stress resistance, may be a key regulator of vascular aging.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
caloric restriction is a potent anti-aging agent that can be exploited to delay the development and progression of vascular aging.
caloric restriction is a potent antiaging intervention and that it is likely to delay vascular aging by increasing bioavailability of NO and suppressing vascular reactive oxygen species formation.

caloric restriction is an effective antiaging intervention that delays the development of vascular aging and cardiovascular disease by attenuating oxidative stress and inflammation, and that the mechanisms underlying these effects are likely to be mediated by the plasma membrane redov system and the NO/cyclic guanosine monophosphate pathway.
The main takeaway from our work is that
caloric restriction may be a powerful intervention to slow aging-related vascular disease.
caloric restriction may be an important tool in preventing vascular aging.
caloric restriction may exert antiaging and antiatherogenic effects by increasing the resistance of cells, tissues, and organs to oxidative stress.
